frequency_question: How often do statutorily mandated congressional resolutions of disapproval successfully pass both chambers and take effect despite executive opposition?
membership_rule: Includes all joint resolutions introduced under fast-track statutory disapproval procedures for major international nuclear or defense sales/agreements where the executive supported the agreement; excludes simple or concurrent resolutions which lack legal effect, and excludes measures that failed to reach a floor vote due to leadership intervention.

cases.name: 1981 AWACS Saudi Arabia Sale Disapproval (Senate passed, House defeated)
2015 Iran Nuclear Agreement (JCPOA) Joint Resolution of Disapproval (filibustered in Senate)
2019 Yemen/Saudi Arms Sales Joint Resolutions of Disapproval (Vetoed, veto sustained)

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 major historical showdowns identified under specific statutory nuclear/arms export disapproval frameworks; all resulted in executive survival via Senate filibuster, chamber split, or sustained veto.
known_gaps: Excludes informal non-statutory resolutions or minor tech transfers not subjected to formal joint resolution disapproval fast-track clocks.
skeleton: Statutory fast-track disapproval mechanisms enacted since 1977 governing executive-branch nuclear and major arms agreements, divided by ultimate success in overriding or preventing executive action.
multiplier: 0 successful veto-proof overrides or unvetoed joint resolutions out of 3 major historical legislative showdowns over Middle East nuclear/arms cooperation.
validity_reason: Statutory frameworks under the Atomic Energy Act and Arms Export Control Act remain stable across decades unless Congress amends the underlying statutory threshold for legislative vetoes.
